title: Go: Buffered Channels
description: Explore buffered channels — channels with capacity that allow non-blocking sends up to a limit.

steps.title: Create a buffered channel
steps.description: Use `make(chan int, 3)` to create a buffered channel of integers with capacity 3. Print the channel using `fmt.Printf("cap: %d\n", cap(ch))`.
hints: Use `make(chan T, N)` where N is the capacity
`len(ch)` returns the current number of elements in the buffer

verification.failureMessage: Make sure to pass the capacity argument to make.

steps.title: Send until full
steps.description: Send 3 integers (10, 20, 30) into a buffered channel of capacity 3 WITHOUT a separate goroutine. Then read and print them. Add a 4th send to observe the blocking/deadlock.
hints: Sends to a buffered channel only block when the buffer is full
Try sending the 4th value without a receiver to see the deadlock
Remove or guard the 4th send to let the program complete

verification.successMessage: You filled the buffer without blocking!
verification.failureMessage: Print the received values to verify the sends worked.

steps.title: Receive from buffered
steps.description: Create a buffered channel of strings with capacity 2. Send "apple" and "banana". Receive both values and print each on its own line.

verification.successMessage: Strings received in FIFO order from the buffered channel!
verification.failureMessage: Receive both values and print them.

steps.title: Check length and capacity
steps.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 5. Send 3 values, then print `len(ch)` and `cap(ch)` after each send to show buffer filling up.
hints: `len(ch)` returns the current buffer fill level
`cap(ch)` is constant and equals the make capacity
Print after each send: `fmt.Printf("len=%d cap=%d\n", len(ch), cap(ch))`

verification.successMessage: You monitored buffer utilization with len and cap!
verification.failureMessage: Print len and cap after the third send.

steps.title: Range over buffered channel
steps.description: Send 5 integers (1 to 5) on a buffered channel, then close it. Use `for v := range ch` to iterate and print each value.
hints: Close the channel with `close(ch)` after all sends
`for v := range ch` reads until the channel is closed
You must close the channel or range will deadlock

verification.successMessage: You ranged over a closed buffered channel perfectly!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure to close the channel before ranging over it.
